Title: TinyML Based Edge Intelligent English Classroom Quality Assessment Scheme

TinyML Based Edge Intelligent English Classroom Quality
Assessment Scheme

ABSTRACT
With the escalating demand for intelligent educational evaluation driven by the advancement of artificial intelligence and edge
computing, traditional English classroom quality assessment methods, characterized by subjectivity, inefficiency, and lack of
real-time feedback, struggle to meet modern educational needs. Moreover, cloud-based AI solutions pose risks to student data
privacy and suffer from high latency. TinyML, a lightweight machine learning paradigm, is inherently compatible with edge intel-
ligence due to its ability to run efficiently on resource-constrained edge devices and perform local inference, thereby reducing
latency and safeguarding data privacy. This paper presents an edge-intelligently assisted English classroom quality evaluation
scheme based on the TinyML model, which utilizes edge computing devices to analyze classroom interaction data in real time,
improving the objectivity and timeliness of teaching quality assessment. The scheme employs lightweight deep learning mod-
els for various analyses and conducts localized data processing to avoid cloud-related issues. Experimental results demonstrate
its superiority over traditional cloud AI schemes in accuracy, real-time performance, and resource utilization, offering a viable
approach for intelligent education evaluation.

Introduction
The traditional English classroom quality evaluation method has
exposed many limitations in long-term practice. The evaluation
of English classroom teaching quality usually relies on expert
attendance or questionnaire survey, which has the problems of
strong subjectivity and low efficiency [1]. These are not con-
ducive to the cultivation of students’ comprehensive language
ability and autonomous learning ability. However, there are
still some shortcomings in the existing classroom evaluation
schemes. In terms of data collection, most of them rely on
manual observation and simple questionnaire survey; the com-
prehensiveness and accuracy of data are limited, and it is difficult
to obtain various information in the classroom in real time and
dynamically. In terms of evaluation models, traditional evalua-
tion models are often based on a fixed index system and weight

teaching scenarios, and cannot fully mine the potential informa-

existing schemes in data privacy protection are relatively weak.
With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and Inter-
net of Things technology, edge intelligence as an emerging com-
puting model has gradually emerged in the field of education
[2]. Edge intelligence emphasizes data processing and analy-
sis on edge devices close to data sources, which can effectively

and protect data privacy [3]. As one of the key technologies of
edge intelligence, the TinyML model is specifically designed for
resource-constrained edge devices [4], which can run machine

learning algorithms on small devices such as microcontrollers
and Internet of Things (IOT) sensors to realize real-time analy-

the characteristics of low power consumption, small size, and fast

in educational scenarios, and provides new ideas and methods for
English classroom quality evaluation [6]. It is of great practical
significance and urgent demand to introduce the TinyML model
and edge intelligence into English classroom quality evaluation.
This work aims to use a TinyML model to realize edge
intelligence-assisted English classroom quality evaluation, and
construct a comprehensive, accurate, real-time, and personalized
evaluation scheme to provide strong support for English teaching.
The specific contributions of this paper are as follows:
• Multi-source data fusion analysis: Collect multi-modal data
in the English classroom, use the TinyML model to per-
form real-time fusion analysis on edge devices, and mine stu-
dents’ learning status and classroom teaching effect reflected
behind the data.
• Real-time dynamic evaluation feedback: With the help of the
real-time processing ability of edge intelligence, the TinyML
model is used to analyze English classroom data in real time,
and real-time evaluation feedback is provided for teachers
and students.
• Reduce costs and protect privacy: TinyML model is deployed
on edge devices to reduce the demand for data transmis-
sion to the cloud, reduce data processing costs, and network
bandwidth pressure.
It is worth noting that this study presents notable improve-
ments in model architecture, compression strategies, and system
deployment. A lightweight neural network structure compatible
with multimodal inputs is designed to enhance the understand-
ing of classroom scenarios. In addition, by integrating compres-
sion techniques such as quantization, pruning, and knowledge
distillation, the model achieves efficient performance on edge
devices. Regarding system deployment, a real-time evaluation
system is developed for embedded terminals, balancing response
speed and data privacy, and significantly enhancing the practical-
ity and intelligence of classroom quality assessment.
The rest part of this paper is organized as follows: Section 2
presents the related theories and techniques used in this paper;
Section 3 constructs the edge intelligent assisted English class-
room quality evaluation scheme based on TinyML; Section 4
gives the experimental and simulation verification of our scheme;
Section 5 provides the conclusion and discussion.

Related Theories and Techniques
English classroom Quality assessment: As a key link in the process
of English teaching, English classroom quality evaluation pro-
vides a strong basis for teaching improvement and student devel-
opment. Currently, there are still some challenges in the practical
application of English classroom quality assessment [7]. The sci-
entificity and comprehensiveness of the evaluation indexes need
to be further improved. Some evaluation indexes may focus too
much on the examination of knowledge and skills, and ignore the
comprehensive quality and personality development of students
[8]. To solve these problems, it is necessary to constantly explore
and innovate the methods and technologies of English classroom
quality evaluation, introduce a more scientific, objective, and
comprehensive evaluation index system, and use advanced edu-
cational technology to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the
evaluation [9].
TinyML technology: As the core supporting technology of edge
intelligence, the TinyML model is designed specifically for
resource-constrained edge devices, which can efficiently run
machine learning algorithms on hardware platforms with limited
memory, computing power, and power consumption, and realize
real-time analysis and processing of English classroom data [10].
Modern TinyML model compression techniques mainly contain
three dimensions of innovation: (1) Yu et al. [11] proposed a pro-
gressive pruning algorithm based on Hessian trajectory. Com-
pared with traditional amplitude pruning, it achieves an addi-
tional 23% sparsity boost on the ESP32 platform. (2) Liu et al. [12]
proposed the AdaQuant algorithm by analyzing the sensitivity
differences between layers to achieve 4–8 bit dynamic bit width
allocation, It reduces the model size by 42% with < 1% accuracy
loss. (3) Wang et al. [13] show that using a logarithmic temper-
ature decay strategy, it can improve the accuracy of the student
model by 2.3 percentage points.
The deployment and operation of TinyML model on edge devices
also face many challenges and require corresponding technical
support. Edge devices have limited hardware resources, such as
small memory, weak computing power, and limited power con-
sumption, so it is necessary to adapt and optimize the model for
different hardware platforms.

The TinyML-Based Edge Intelligent
Assisted English Classroom Quality Evaluation
Scheme
This section gives the overall architecture of the edge intelligently
assisted English classroom quality evaluation scheme based on
the TinyML model. The architecture is mainly composed of three
core parts: edge device layer, network transport layer, and cloud
management layer. All parts cooperate closely to build an efficient
and intelligent English classroom quality evaluation system.
• Edge device layer: As the front-end of data collection, the
edge device layer is deployed in various key locations of the
English classroom and is responsible for collecting multi-
modal data of students in the classroom in real time. These
devices include smart cameras, microphone arrays, etc.,
and they each perform their own duties to obtain informa-
tion about students’ classroom performance from different
dimensions.
• The network transport layer: The network transport layer
is responsible for transferring the data collected by edge
devices to the cloud management layer safely and efficiently
or exchanging data between edge devices. Considering the
complexity of the English classroom environment and the
real-time requirements of data transmission, this scheme
uses a combination of multiple transmission technologies.
• Cloud management: The cloud management layer is the core
control and data analysis center of the whole system, which
undertakes important tasks such as data storage, model
training, evaluation and analysis, and result display. In terms
of data storage, the distributed database Hadoop Distributed
File System (HDFS) and NoSQL database are used to effi-
ciently store and manage massive English classroom data.
To ensure the privacy and security of teachers and students, the
system adopts an edge computing architecture, where data pre-
processing and model inference are performed locally on the ter-
minal devices, eliminating the need to upload raw data to the
cloud. Additionally, techniques such as data desensitization (e.g.,
face blurring, voice anonymization) and local encrypted storage
are implemented to secure data throughout collection, process-
ing, and storage. This approach not only reduces the risk of data
leakage but also enhances user trust, meeting the high privacy
standards required in educational settings.

The vision module uses the Sony IMX477 RGB-IR sensor, which

The hardware selection of the edge computing layer is carefully
considered. The main processor is Rockchip RK3588, which has
an NPU computing power of up to 6TOPS, and can efficiently
process complex machine learning tasks. ESP32-S3 is used as
the coprocessor, which supports vector instruction expansion
to accelerate specific computing tasks. In order to ensure the
real-time performance of edge devices under multi-task process-
ing, a mixed-criticality scheduling strategy is used, which can rea-
sonably allocate computing resources according to the criticality
and real-time requirements of tasks, and reduce the overall power
consumption while ensuring the response speed of the system.
The cloud management platform is built on Kubernetes, which
realizes elastic container deployment and can dynamically adjust
computing resources according to business needs to improve
resource utilization. At the same time, Apache Arrow format is
used to realize zero-copy data transmission between the edge and
the cloud, which avoids the copy overhead of data in the trans-
mission process, greatly improves the efficiency of data transmis-
sion and provides strong support for subsequent data analysis and
model training.

The coefficient can capture the second-order change trend
of speech features and enhance the sensitivity to emotional

matone filter (Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients) are
introduced, which are more in line with the human auditory

In the design of lightweight model architecture, MobileNetV3
improved by GhostModule is used as the backbone network.
GhostModule achieves similar feature extraction effects as tra-
ditional convolution with fewer parameters and calculations,
which effectively reduces the number of model parameters. In
order to process streaming speech input, a Causal Conv1D layer
is added to the network to ensure that the model only relies on
the past and current speech information when predicting the cur-
rent emotion, which is consistent with the actual speech process-
ing logic. The output layer designs the emotion-semantic joint
embedding space, which maps the emotional and semantic infor-
mation of speech into the same space to achieve more accurate
emotion recognition.
In the quantization deployment step, a mixed precision quanti-
zation strategy guided by hierarchical sensitivity is implemented.
According to the sensitivity of each layer of the network to quan-
tization, different weights and activation bit widths are set for dif-
ferent layers. For example, convolutional layers 1–3 employ 8 bit
weights and 8 bit activations, depthwise separable layers use 4 bit
weights and 6 bit activations, and fully connected layers keep 8 bit
weights and 8 bit activations. This quantization method greatly
reduces the storage space and calculation amount of the model
under the premise of ensuring minimal loss of model accuracy,
so that it can adapt to the resource limitations of edge devices.

Experimental Verification of the Scheme
4.1
|
Experimental Environment
The above scheme focuses on the quality evaluation of the
English classroom, integrates TinyML and edge intelligence tech-
nology, and its hardware and software environment design is
designed to ensure the efficient operation of the system. On the
hardware side, it includes a variety of sensing and computing
devices, and on the software side, it includes various algorithm
libraries and development frameworks. The hardware details are
as follows:
• Terminal perception layer: We adopt Infineon IM69D130
MEMS microphone array as the speech acquisition device,
which had a high signal-to-noise ratio of 69 dB to accurately
collect classroom speech data, and used STM32H743 as the
front-end processor to realize the real-time beamforming
function.
• Edge computing layer: The main processor of this paper
is Rockchip RK3588 with 6TOPS NPU computing power,
which is used to efficiently process complex machine learn-
ing tasks. The coprocessor leverages ESP32-S3, the support
Vector Instruction extension, to accelerate specific computa-
tional tasks.
• Visual processing unit: In this paper, we adopt the NVIDIA
Jetson Orin Nano (8GB) to process the 1080p@30fps video
stream and run the YOLOv8 pose estimation model.
The operating system used for the experiments in this paper
is Ubuntu 22.04 LTS + RT-Preempt patch (𝜇s scheduling delay).
The inference framework we used Lite 2.15 (supports INT4 quan-
tization). The communication protocol we used is MQTT over
TLS 1.3 (message throughput ≥500msg∕s).
To further align with edge hardware, we adopted hardware-aware
training, fine-tuning the loss function to mitigate accuracy loss
from quantization and pruning. The model is optimized for plat-
forms like ARM Cortex-M and ESP32, using mixed-precision
quantization (INT4/INT8). Additionally, we explored feder-
ated learning for on-device updates without data upload,
and employed compiler-level tuning (e.g., CMSIS-NN, TVM)
to reduce latency and power consumption. These strategies
enhance deployment adaptability and efficiency.
4.2
|
The Experimental and Simulation
Verification
This experiment selects three schools at different levels, a total
of 15 English classes as the research objects, covering junior
high school and senior high school, with a total number of more
than 600 students and 20 teachers. The experimental period is
12 weeks. The experimental group (using this scheme) and the
control group (using the traditional classroom quality evaluation
method) are set up to strictly control the teaching content, teacher
qualifications, and other variables of the two groups. To ensure
experimental rigor, the control group received no technical inter-
vention throughout the 12 weeks. Classes were selected from
schools with similar academic levels, and groups were balanced
in terms of student performance, class size, and teacher style.
All teachers followed the same curriculum, with only the exper-
imental group using the intelligent system, minimizing external
influences.
After 12 weeks of experiment, the average English score of the
experimental group students increased by 12.3 points, signifi-
cantly higher than the control group’s 5.6 points. At the same
time, through classroom observation and student questionnaire
feedback, the participation of students in the experimental group
in the classroom has increased by 35%, and the frequency of
teacher-student interaction has increased by 40%, which indi-
cates that this scheme can effectively promote the improvement
of English classroom teaching quality. The experimental results
are shown in Table 1.
To further validate the significance of the improvement in
teaching effectiveness, we conducted a paired sample t-test on
the pre-test and post-test scores of the experimental and con-
trol groups shown in Table 1. The results indicate that the
improvement in the experimental group is statistically significant
(p < 0.01), while the change in the control group is not signifi-
cant (p > 0.05). This demonstrates that the proposed system has
a significant positive impact on enhancing classroom teaching
quality, and the data is statistically well supported.

Conclusion
This paper focuses on the pain points of English classroom
quality evaluation, our scheme deeply integrates TinyML model
and edge intelligence technology to build an efficient, accu-
rate and real-time intelligent evaluation system. Through the
three-tier collaborative architecture design of “end edge cloud”,
the real-time collection, local processing and cloud optimization
of multimodal data are realized, and the system response speed
is significantly improved while ensuring data privacy.
However, there is still room for optimization. Future research
will focus on further improving the adaptability of the model to
complex teaching scenarios, exploring more efficient federated
learning strategies to reduce model update time, optimizing hard-
ware and software collaboration, and reducing system deploy-
ment costs. The successful practice of this program provides a
new paradigm for the in-depth application of edge intelligent
technology in the field of education, which is expected to promote
the innovative development of intelligent education.

Abstract: With the escalating demand for intelligent educational evaluation driven by the advancement of artificial intelligence and edge computing, traditional English classroom quality assessment methods, characterized by subjectivity, inefficiency, and lack of real-time feedback, struggle to meet modern educational needs. Moreover, cloud-based AI solutions pose risks to student data privacy and suffer from high latency. TinyML, a lightweight machine learning paradigm, is inherently compatible with edge intel- ligence due to its ability to run efficiently on resource-constrained edge devices and perform local inference, thereby reducing latency and safeguarding data privacy. This paper presents an edge-intelligently assisted English classroom quality evaluation scheme based on the TinyML model, which utilizes edge computing devices to analyze classroom interaction data in real time, improving the objectivity and timeliness of teaching quality assessment. The scheme employs lightweight deep learning mod- els for various analyses and conducts localized data processing to avoid cloud-related issues. Experimental results demonstrate its superiority over traditional cloud AI schemes in accuracy, real-time performance, and resource utilization, offering a viable approach for intelligent education evaluation.
